newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN's Liberia observers' mission extended four months.
newsitem.headline: UN's Liberia observers' mission extended four months.

text.p: The Security Council on Wednesday unanimously extended for four months the mission of a 23-member military observer group in Liberia.
The U.N. group will stay in the nation, which has been torn by civil war, until March 31, 1997.
The U.N. Observer Mission in Liberia works with ECOMOG, the 7,500-strong force of the Economic Community of West African States.

The council also condemned "in the strongest possible terms the practice of recruiting, training and deploying children for combat." It demanded that parties to the 7-year-old, multi-sided conflict "immediately cease this inhumane and abhorrent activity" and release all child soldiers for demobilization.
And it condemned all attacks on personnel of the observer group, ECOMOG and international organisations delivering humanitarian aid.

The resolution stressed what it said was the obligation of all states to comply strictly with an embargo on the delivery of weapons and military equipment to Liberia imposed by the Security Council in November 1992.
More than 150,000 people have been killed since the civil war erupted in December 1989, devastating Liberia's mining and rubber economy. There have been more than a dozen shattered peace accords.
The latest agreement, signed in Abuja, Nigeria, in August, calls for disarmament and the holding of elections at the end of May 1997.

Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, in a recent report, said that while there had "recently been some positive developments, the entrenched hostility and mistrust that have resulted from this protracted conflict continues to pose a threat to the peace process in Liberia."

The latest resolution asked Boutros-Ghali to keep the council informed of progress on disarmament and demobilization and submit a report by Jan. 31, 1997, with recommendations about possible U.N. support for elections.
